AM_boost_medium_cnn_budget10.verdict: Outcome C: min_x rises ~9% at m=2 and ~13% at m=64, Y RISES (not falls), eta ~flat. A reachable higher-min_x point exists that the adaptive_index controller does not use. Improvement is modest and saturates after m=2 -> achievable region has limited but non-zero curvature.

final_answer: The near-rectangular AUC frontier is PARTLY a controller-allocation artifact and PARTLY a genuine structural property. Boosting the true bottleneck class (medium_cnn_summarize) reaches an operating point ~10-13% higher in system min_x with NO goodput loss - a point the current virtual-queue/index controller does not find. But the reachable gain is small and saturates immediately (one discrete step at m=2), so the achievable region is close to rectangular, not a rich smooth trade-off. Recommendation: fix the controller allocation (the weighted_utility ranking weight x expected_useful_tokens structurally underweights low-acceptance clients, i.e. exactly the group that sets the interactivity floor; Z_i is not compensating enough), but do not expect a large AUC gain at this N/gamma_max scale.
